correctness.rationale: Equation (2.12) of arXiv:2606.06655 is checked by 126 independent rational-series computations. The substitution \(x=ze^{-u}, y=e^{2u}\) gives the derivative identity for \(\mathbb E[(2N-\tau)z^{\tau}]\). Absolutely convergent Fubini follows from \(|2N-\tau|/\tau\le1\), giving \(q-1/2\) as an integral with sign kernel \(H(2/z)\). If \(k\) is the largest imbalanced border, complement so \(d_k\ge1\); for smaller \(j\), the binary prefix imbalance obeys \(d_j\ge1-(k-j)\). The lower envelope \(F_k(t)=t^k-\sum_{j=1}^{k-2}(k-j-1)t^j\) satisfies \((t-1)^2F_k(t)=(t-2)t^{k+1}+(k-1)t^2-(k-2)t>0\) for \(t\ge2\). Thus all integrands share the sign of \(d_k\), while balanced borders yield equality. 2,046 numerical sign comparisons and separate hitting-state recurrences corroborate, not replace, the infinite proof.
